exact_text: The ratifications shall be deposited with the Government of the United States of America, which shall notify all the signatory states of each deposit as well as the Secretary-General of the Organization when he has been appointed.

structural_path: Charter of the United Nations › Chapter XIX: Ratification and Signature › Article 110 › ¶3
exact_text: The present Charter shall come into force upon the deposit of ratifications by the Republic of China, France, the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, and the United States of America, and by a majority of the other signatory states. A protocol of the ratifications deposited shall thereupon be drawn up by the Government of the United States of America which shall communicate copies thereof to all the signatory states.

structural_path: Charter of the United Nations › Chapter XIX: Ratification and Signature › Article 110 › ¶4
exact_text: The states signatory to the present Charter which ratify it after it has come into force will become original Members of the United Nations on the date of the deposit of their respective ratifications.

structural_path: Charter of the United Nations › Chapter XIX: Ratification and Signature › Article 111
exact_text: The present Charter, of which the Chinese, French, Russian, English, and Spanish texts are equally authentic, shall remain deposited in the archives of the Government of the United States of America. Duly certified copies thereof shall be transmitted by that Government to the Governments of the other signatory states.

structural_path: Charter of the United Nations › Chapter XIX: Ratification and Signature › Article 111
exact_text: In Faith Whereof the representatives of the Governments of the United Nations have signed the present Charter. DONE at the city of San Francisco the twenty-sixth day of June, one thousand nine hundred and forty-five.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Article 1
exact_text: The International Court of Justice established by the Charter of the United Nations as the principal judicial organ of the United Nations shall be constituted and shall function in accordance with the provisions of the present Statute.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 2
exact_text: The Court shall be composed of a body of independent judges, elected regardless of their nationality from among persons of high moral character, who possess the qualifications required in their respective countries for appointment to the highest judicial offices, or are jurisconsults of recognized competence in international law.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 3 › ¶1
exact_text: The Court shall consist of fifteen Members, no two of whom may be nationals of the same State.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 3 › ¶2
exact_text: A person who for the purposes of membership in the Court could be regarded as a national of more than one State shall be deemed to be a national of the one in which he ordinarily exercises civil and political rights.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 4 › ¶1
exact_text: The Members of the Court shall be elected by the General Assembly and by the Security Council from a list of persons nominated by the national groups in the Permanent Court of Arbitration, in accordance with the following provisions.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 4 › ¶2
exact_text: In the case of Members of the United Nations not represented in the Permanent Court of Arbitration, candidates shall be nominated by national groups appointed for this purpose by their governments under the same conditions as those prescribed for members of the Permanent Court of Arbitration by Article 44 of the Convention of The Hague of 1907 for the pacific settlement of international disputes.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 4 › ¶3
exact_text: The conditions under which a State which is a party to the present Statute but is not a Member of the United Nations may participate in electing the Members of the Court shall, in the absence of a special agreement, be laid down by the General Assembly upon recommendation of the Security Council.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 5 › ¶1
exact_text: At least three months before the date of the election, the Secretary-General of the United Nations shall address a written request to the members of the Permanent Court of Arbitration belonging to the States which are parties to the present Statute, and to the members of the national groups appointed under Article 4, paragraph 2, inviting them to undertake, within a given time, by national groups, the nomination of persons in a position to accept the duties of a Member of the Court.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 5 › ¶2
exact_text: No group may nominate more than four persons, not more than two of whom shall be of their own nationality. In no case may the number of candidates nominated by a group be more than double the number of seats to be filled.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 6
exact_text: Before making these nominations, each national group is recommended to consult its highest court of justice, its legal faculties and schools of law, and its national academies and national sections of international academies devoted to the study of law.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 7 › ¶1
exact_text: The Secretary-General shall prepare a list in alphabetical order of all the persons thus nominated. Save as provided in Article 12, paragraph 2, these shall be the only persons eligible.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 7 › ¶2
exact_text: The Secretary-General shall submit this list to the General Assembly and to the Security Council.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 8
exact_text: The General Assembly and the Security Council shall proceed independently of one another to elect the members of the Court.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 9
exact_text: At every election, the electors shall bear in mind not only that the persons to be elected should individually possess the qualifications required, but also that in the body as a whole the representation of the main forms of civilization and of the principal legal systems of the world should be assured.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 10 › ¶1
exact_text: Those candidates who obtain an absolute majority of votes in the General Assembly and in the Security Council shall be considered as elected.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 10 › ¶2
exact_text: Any vote of the Security Council, whether for the election of judges or for the appointment of members of the conference envisaged in Article 12, shall be taken without any distinction between permanent and non-permanent members of the Security Council.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 10 › ¶3
exact_text: In the event of more than one national of the same state obtaining an absolute majority of the votes both of the General Assembly and of the Security Council, the eldest of these only shall be considered as elected.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 11
exact_text: If, after the first meeting held for the purpose of the election, one or more seats remain to be filled, a second and, if necessary, a third meeting shall take place.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 12 › ¶1
exact_text: If, after the third meeting, one or more seats still remain unfilled, a joint conference consisting of six members, three appointed by the General Assembly and three by the Security Council, may be formed at any time at the request of either the General Assembly or the Security Council, for the purpose of choosing by the vote of an absolute majority one name for each seat still vacant, to submit to the General Assembly and the Security Council for their respective acceptance.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 12 › ¶2
exact_text: If the joint conference is unanimously agreed upon any person who fulfills the required conditions, he may be included in its list, even though he was not included in the list of nominations referred to in Article 7.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 12 › ¶3
exact_text: If the joint conference is satisfied that it will not be successful in procuring an election, those members of the Court who have already been elected shall, within a period to be fixed by the Security Council, proceed to fill the vacant seats by selection from among those candidates who have obtained votes either in the General Assembly or in the Security Council.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 12 › ¶4
exact_text: In the event of an equality of votes among the judges, the eldest judge shall have a casting vote.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 13 › ¶1
exact_text: The members of the Court shall be elected for nine years and may be re-elected; provided, however, that of the judges elected at the first election, the terms of five judges shall expire at the end of three years and the terms of five more judges shall expire at the end of six years.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 13 › ¶2
exact_text: The judges whose terms are to expire at the end of the above-mentioned initial periods of three and six years shall be chosen by lot to be drawn by the Secretary-General immediately after the first election has been completed.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 13 › ¶3
exact_text: The members of the Court shall continue to discharge their duties until their places have been filled. Though replaced, they shall finish any cases which they may have begun.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 13 › ¶4
exact_text: In the case of the resignation of a member of the Court, the resignation shall be addressed to the President of the Court for transmission to the Secretary-General. This last notification makes the place vacant.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 14
exact_text: Vacancies shall be filled by the same method as that laid down for the first election, subject to the following provision: the Secretary-General shall, within one month of the occurrence of the vacancy, proceed to issue the invitations provided for in Article 5, and the date of the election shall be fixed by the Security Council.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 15
exact_text: A member of the Court elected to replace a member whose term of office has not expired shall hold office for the remainder of his predecessor's term.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 16 › ¶1
exact_text: No member of the Court may exercise any political or administrative function, or engage in any other occupation of a professional nature.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 16 › ¶2
exact_text: Any doubt on this point shall be settled by the decision of the Court.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 17 › ¶1
exact_text: No member of the Court may act as agent, counsel, or advocate in any case.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 17 › ¶2
exact_text: No member may participate in the decision of any case in which he has previously taken part as agent, counsel, or advocate for one of the parties, or as a member of a national or international court, or of a commission of enquiry, or in any other capacity.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 17 › ¶3
exact_text: Any doubt on this point shall be settled by the decision of the Court.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 18 › ¶1
exact_text: No member of the Court can be dismissed unless, in the unanimous opinion of the other members, he has ceased to fulfill the required conditions.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 18 › ¶2
exact_text: Formal notification thereof shall be made to the Secretary-General by the Registrar.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 18 › ¶3
exact_text: This notification makes the place vacant.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 19
exact_text: The members of the Court, when engaged on the business of the Court, shall enjoy diplomatic privileges and immunities.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 20
exact_text: Every member of the Court shall, before taking up his duties, make a solemn declaration in open court that he will exercise his powers impartially and conscientiously.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 21 › ¶1
exact_text: The Court shall elect its President and Vice-President for three years; they may be re-elected.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 21 › ¶2
exact_text: The Court shall appoint its Registrar and may provide for the appointment of such other officers as may be necessary.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 22 › ¶1
exact_text: The seat of the Court shall be established at The Hague. This, however, shall not prevent the Court from sitting and exercising its functions elsewhere whenever the Court considers it desirable.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 22 › ¶2
exact_text: The President and the Registrar shall reside at the seat of the Court.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 23 › ¶1
exact_text: The Court shall remain permanently in session, except during the judicial vacations, the dates and duration of which shall be fixed by the Court.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 23 › ¶2
exact_text: Members of the Court are entitled to periodic leave, the dates and duration of which shall be fixed by the Court, having in mind the distance between The Hague and the home of each judge.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 23 › ¶3
exact_text: Members of the Court shall be bound, unless they are on leave or prevented from attending by illness or other serious reasons duly explained to the President, to hold themselves permanently at the disposal of the Court.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 24 › ¶1
exact_text: If, for some special reason, a member of the Court considers that he should not take part in the decision of a particular case, he shall so inform the President.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 24 › ¶2
exact_text: If the President considers that for some special reason one of the members of the Court should not sit in a particular case, he shall give him notice accordingly.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 24 › ¶3
exact_text: If in any such case the member of the Court and the President disagree, the matter shall be settled by the decision of the Court.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 25 › ¶1
exact_text: The full Court shall sit except when it is expressly provided otherwise in the present Statute.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 25 › ¶2
exact_text: Subject to the condition that the number of judges available to constitute the Court is not thereby reduced below eleven, the Rules of the Court may provide for allowing one or more judges, according to circumstances and in rotation, to be dispensed from sitting.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 25 › ¶3
exact_text: A quorum of nine judges shall suffice to constitute the Court.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 26 › ¶1
exact_text: The Court may from time to time form one or more chambers, composed of three or more judges as the Court may determine, for dealing with particular categories of cases; for example, labour cases and cases relating to transit and communications.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 26 › ¶2
exact_text: The Court may at any time form a chamber for dealing with a particular case. The number of judges to constitute such a chamber shall be determined by the Court with the approval of the parties.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 26 › ¶3
exact_text: Cases shall be heard and determined by the chambers provided for in this article if the parties so request.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 27
exact_text: A judgment given by any of the chambers provided for in Articles 26 and 29 shall be considered as rendered by the Court.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 28
exact_text: The chambers provided for in Articles 26 and 29 may, with the consent of the parties, sit and exercise their functions elsewhere than at The Hague.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 29
exact_text: With a view to the speedy dispatch of business, the Court shall form annually a chamber composed of five judges which, at the request of the parties, may hear and determine cases by summary procedure. In addition, two judges shall be selected for the purpose of replacing judges who find it impossible to sit.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 30 › ¶1
exact_text: The Court shall frame rules for carrying out its functions. In particular, it shall lay down rules of procedure.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 30 › ¶2
exact_text: The Rules of the Court may provide for assessors to sit with the Court or with any of its chambers, without the right to vote.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 31 › ¶1
exact_text: Judges of the nationality of each of the parties shall retain their right to sit in the case before the Court.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 31 › ¶2
exact_text: If the Court includes upon the Bench a judge of the nationality of one of the parties, any other party may choose a person to sit as judge. Such person shall be chosen preferably from among those persons who have been nominated as candidates as provided in Articles 4 and 5.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 31 › ¶3
exact_text: If the Court includes upon the Bench no judge of the nationality of the parties, each of these parties may proceed to choose a judge as provided in paragraph 2 of this Article.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 31 › ¶4
exact_text: The provisions of this Article shall apply to the case of Articles 26 and 29. In such cases, the President shall request one or, if necessary, two of the members of the Court forming the chamber to give place to the members of the Court of the nationality of the parties concerned, and, failing such, or if they are unable to be present, to the judges specially chosen by the parties.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 31 › ¶5
exact_text: Should there be several parties in the same interest, they shall, for the purpose of the preceding provisions, be reckoned as one party only. Any doubt upon this point shall be settled by the decision of the Court.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 31 › ¶6
exact_text: Judges chosen as laid down in paragraphs 2, 3, and 4 of this Article shall fulfill the conditions required by Articles 2, 17 (paragraph 2), 20, and 24 of the present Statute. They shall take part in the decision on terms of complete equality with their colleagues.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 32 › ¶1
exact_text: Each member of the Court shall receive an annual salary.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 32 › ¶2
exact_text: The President shall receive a special annual allowance.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 32 › ¶3
exact_text: The Vice-President shall receive a special allowance for every day on which he acts as President.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 32 › ¶4
exact_text: The judges chosen under Article 31, other than members of the Court, shall receive compensation for each day on which they exercise their functions.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 32 › ¶5
exact_text: These salaries, allowances, and compensation shall be fixed by the General Assembly. They may not be decreased during the term of office.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 32 › ¶6
exact_text: The salary of the Registrar shall be fixed by the General Assembly on the proposal of the Court.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 32 › ¶7
exact_text: Regulations made by the General Assembly shall fix the conditions under which retirement pensions may be given to members of the Court and to the Registrar, and the conditions under which members of the Court and the Registrar shall have their travelling expenses refunded.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 32 › ¶8
exact_text: The above salaries, allowances, and compensation shall be free of all taxation.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter I: Organization Of The Court › Article 33
exact_text: The expenses of the Court shall be borne by the United Nations in such a manner as shall be decided by the General Assembly.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter II: Competence Of The Court › Article 34 › ¶1
exact_text: Only states may be parties in cases before the Court.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter II: Competence Of The Court › Article 34 › ¶2
exact_text: The Court, subject to and in conformity with its Rules, may request of public international organizations information relevant to cases before it, and shall receive such information presented by such organizations on their own initiative.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter II: Competence Of The Court › Article 34 › ¶3
exact_text: Whenever the construction of the constituent instrument of a public international organization or of an international convention adopted thereunder is in question in a case before the Court, the Registrar shall so notify the public international organization concerned and shall communicate to it copies of all the written proceedings.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter II: Competence Of The Court › Article 35 › ¶1
exact_text: The Court shall be open to the states parties to the present Statute.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter II: Competence Of The Court › Article 35 › ¶2
exact_text: The conditions under which the Court shall be open to other states shall, subject to the special provisions contained in treaties in force, be laid down by the Security Council, but in no case shall such conditions place the parties in a position of inequality before the Court.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter II: Competence Of The Court › Article 35 › ¶3
exact_text: When a state which is not a Member of the United Nations is a party to a case, the Court shall fix the amount which that party is to contribute towards the expenses of the Court. This provision shall not apply if such state is bearing a share of the expenses of the Court

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter II: Competence Of The Court › Article 36 › ¶1
exact_text: The jurisdiction of the Court comprises all cases which the parties refer to it and all matters specially provided for in the Charter of the United Nations or in treaties and conventions in force.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter II: Competence Of The Court › Article 36 › ¶2
Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter II: Competence Of The Court › Article 36 › ¶3
exact_text: The declarations referred to above may be made unconditionally or on condition of reciprocity on the part of several or certain states, or for a certain time.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter II: Competence Of The Court › Article 36 › ¶4
exact_text: Such declarations shall be deposited with the Secretary-General of the United Nations, who shall transmit copies thereof to the parties to the Statute and to the Registrar of the Court.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter II: Competence Of The Court › Article 36 › ¶5
exact_text: Declarations made under Article 36 of the Statute of the Permanent Court of International Justice and which are still in force shall be deemed, as between the parties to the present Statute, to be acceptances of the compulsory jurisdiction of the International Court of Justice for the period which they still have to run and in accordance with their terms.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter II: Competence Of The Court › Article 36 › ¶6
exact_text: In the event of a dispute as to whether the Court has jurisdiction, the matter shall be settled by the decision of the Court.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter II: Competence Of The Court › Article 37
exact_text: Whenever a treaty or convention in force provides for reference of a matter to a tribunal to have been instituted by the League of Nations, or to the Permanent Court of International Justice, the matter shall, as between the parties to the present Statute, be referred to the International Court of Justice.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter II: Competence Of The Court › Article 38 › ¶1
Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter II: Competence Of The Court › Article 38 › ¶2
exact_text:
This provision shall not prejudice the power of the Court to decide a case
ex aequo et bono
, if the parties agree thereto.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 39 › ¶1
exact_text: The official languages of the Court shall be French and English. If the parties agree that the case shall be conducted in French, the judgment shall be delivered in French. If the parties agree that the case shall be conducted in English, the judgment shall be delivered in English.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 39 › ¶2
exact_text: In the absence of an agreement as to which language shall be employed, each party may, in the pleadings, use the language which it prefers; the decision of the Court shall be given in French and English. In this case the Court shall at the same time determine which of the two texts shall be considered as authoritative.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 39 › ¶3
exact_text: The Court shall, at the request of any party, authorize a language other than French or English to be used by that party.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 40 › ¶1
exact_text: Cases are brought before the Court, as the case may be, either by the notification of the special agreement or by a written application addressed to the Registrar. In either case the subject of the dispute and the parties shall be indicated.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 40 › ¶2
exact_text: The Registrar shall forthwith communicate the application to all concerned.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 40 › ¶3

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 41 › ¶1
exact_text: The Court shall have the power to indicate, if it considers that circumstances so require, any provisional measures which ought to be taken to preserve the respective rights of either party.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 41 › ¶2
exact_text: Pending the final decision, notice of the measures suggested shall forthwith be given to the parties and to the Security Council.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 42 › ¶1
exact_text: The parties shall be represented by agents.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 42 › ¶2
exact_text: They may have the assistance of counsel or advocates before the Court.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 42 › ¶3
exact_text: The agents, counsel, and advocates of parties before the Court shall enjoy the privileges and immunities necessary to the independent exercise of their duties.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 43 › ¶1
exact_text: The procedure shall consist of two parts: written and oral.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 43 › ¶2
exact_text: The written proceedings shall consist of the communication to the Court and to the parties of memorials, counter-memorials and, if necessary, replies; also all papers and documents in support.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 43 › ¶3
exact_text: These communications shall be made through the Registrar, in the order and within the time fixed by the Court.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 43 › ¶4
exact_text: A certified copy of every document produced by one party shall be communicated to the other party.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 43 › ¶5
exact_text: The oral proceedings shall consist of the hearing by the Court of witnesses, experts, agents, counsel, and advocates.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 44 › ¶1
exact_text: For the service of all notices upon persons other than the agents, counsel, and advocates, the Court shall apply direct to the government of the state upon whose territory the notice has to be served.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 44 › ¶2
exact_text: The same provision shall apply whenever steps are to be taken to procure evidence on the spot.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 45

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 46
exact_text: The hearing in Court shall be public, unless the Court shall decide otherwise, or unless the parties demand that the public be not admitted .

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 47 › ¶1
exact_text: Minutes shall be made at each hearing and signed by the Registrar and the President.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 47 › ¶2
exact_text: These minutes alone shall be authentic.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 48
exact_text: The Court shall make orders for the conduct of the case, shall decide the form and time in which each party must conclude its arguments, and make all arrangements connected with the taking of evidence.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 49
exact_text: The Court may, even before the hearing begins, call upon the agents to produce any document or to supply any explanations. Formal note shall be taken of any refusal.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 50
exact_text: The Court may, at any time, entrust any individual, body, bureau, commission, or other organization that it may select, with the task of carrying out an enquiry or giving an expert opinion.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 51
exact_text: During the hearing any relevant questions are to be put to the witnesses and experts under the conditions laid down by the Court in the rules of procedure referred to in Article 30.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 52
exact_text: After the Court has received the proofs and evidence within the time specified for the purpose, it may refuse to accept any further oral or written evidence that one party may desire to present unless the other side consents.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 53 › ¶1
exact_text: Whenever one of the parties does not appear before the Court, or fails to defend its case, the other party may call upon the Court to decide in favour of its claim.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 54 › ¶1

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 54 › ¶2
exact_text: The Court shall withdraw to consider the judgment.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 54 › ¶3
exact_text: The deliberations of the Court shall take place in private and remain secret.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 55 › ¶1
exact_text: All questions shall be decided by a majority of the judges present.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 55 › ¶2
exact_text: In the event of an equality of votes, the President or the judge who acts in his place shall have a casting vote.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 56 › ¶1
exact_text: The judgment shall state the reasons on which it is based.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 56 › ¶2
exact_text: It shall contain the names of the judges who have taken part in the decision.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 57
exact_text: If the judgment does not represent in whole or in part the unanimous opinion of the judges, any judge shall be entitled to deliver a separate opinion.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 58
exact_text: The judgment shall be signed by the President and by the Registrar. It shall be read in open court, due notice having been given to the agents.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 59
exact_text: The decision of the Court has no binding force except between the parties and in respect of that particular case.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 60

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 61 › ¶2

exact_text: The Court may require previous compliance with the terms of the judgment before it admits proceedings in revision.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 61 › ¶4
exact_text: The application for revision must be made at latest within six months of the discovery of the new fact.

structural_path: Statute of the International Court of Justice › Chapter III: Procedure › Article 61 › ¶5

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 48: Error › ¶1
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Error
exact_text:
A State may invoke an error in a treaty as invalidating its consent to be bound by the treaty if
the error relates to a fact or situ ation which was assumed by that State to exist at the time when the
treaty was concluded and formed an essential basis of its consent to be bound by the treaty.
17

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 48: Error › ¶2
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Error
exact_text:
Paragraph 1 shall not apply if the State in question contributed by its own conduct to the error
or if the circumstances were such as to put that State on notice of a possible error.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 48: Error › ¶3
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Error
exact_text:
An error relating only to the wording of the text of a treaty does not affect its validity; article 79
then applies.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 49: Fraud
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Fraud
exact_text:
If a State has been induced to conclude a treaty by the fraudulent conduct of another negotiating
State, the State may invoke the fraud as invalidating its consent to be bound by the treaty.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 50: Corruption of a representative of a State
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Corruption of a representative of a State
exact_text:
If the expression of a State's consent to be bound by a treaty has been procured through the
corruption of its representative directly or indirectly by another negotiating State, the State may invoke
such corruption as invalidating its consent to be bound by the treaty.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 51: Coercion of a representative of a State
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Coercion of a representative of a State
exact_text:
The expression of a State's consent to be bound by a treaty which has been procured by the
coercion of its representative through acts or threats directed against him shall be without any legal
effect.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 52: Coercion of a State by the threat or use of force
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Coercion of a State by the threat or use of force
exact_text:
A treaty is void if its conclusion has been procured by the threat or use of force in violation of the
principles of international law embodied in the Charter of the United Nations.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 53: Treaties conflicting with a peremptory norm of
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Treaties conflicting with a peremptory norm of
exact_text:
general international law ("jus cogens")
A treaty is void if, at the time of its conclusion , it conflicts with a peremptory norm of general
international law. For the purposes of the present Convention, a peremptory norm of general
international law is a norm accepted and recognized by the international community of States as a whole
as a norm from which no derogation is permitted and which can be modified only by a subsequent norm
of general international law having the same character.
18

OF THE OPERATION OF TREATIES

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 54: Termination of or withdrawal from a treaty under

heading: Termination of or withdrawal from a treaty under
exact_text:
its provisions or by consent of the parties
The termination of a treaty or the withdrawal of a party may take place:
(a) in conformity with the pr ovisions of the treaty; or
(b) at any time by consent of all the parties after consultation with the other contracting States.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 55: Reduction of the parties to a multilateral treaty below the
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Reduction of the parties to a multilateral treaty below the
exact_text:

Unless the treaty otherwise provides, a multilateral treaty does not terminate by reason only of the
fact that the number of the parties falls below the number necessary for its entry into force.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 56: Denunciation of or withdrawal from a treaty containing no

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 56: Denunciation of or withdrawal from a treaty containing no › ¶1
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Denunciation of or withdrawal from a treaty containing no
exact_text:
A treaty which contains no provision regarding its termination and which does not provide for
denunciation or withdrawal is not subject to denunciation or withdrawal unless:
(a) it is established that the parties intended to admit the possibility of denunciation or withdrawal; or
(b) a right of denunciation or withdrawal may be implied by the nature of the treaty.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 56: Denunciation of or withdrawal from a treaty containing no › ¶2
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Denunciation of or withdrawal from a treaty containing no
exact_text:
A party shall give not less than twelve months' notice of its intention to denounce or withdraw
from a treaty under paragraph 1.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 57: Suspension of the operation of a treaty under its
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Suspension of the operation of a treaty under its
exact_text:
provisions or by consent of the parties
The operation of a treaty in regard to all the part ies or to a particular party may be suspended:
(a) in conformity with the pr ovisions of the treaty; or
(b) at any time by consent of all the parties after consultation with the other contracting States.
19

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 58: Suspension of the operation of a multilateral treaty by
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Suspension of the operation of a multilateral treaty by
exact_text: agreement between certain of the parties only

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 58: Suspension of the operation of a multilateral treaty by › ¶1
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Suspension of the operation of a multilateral treaty by
exact_text:
Two or more parties to a multilateral treaty may conclude an agreement to suspend the
operation of provisions of the treaty, temporarily and as between themselves alone, if:
(a) the possibility of such a suspension is provided for by the treaty; or
(b) the suspension in question is no t prohibited by the treaty and:
(i) does not affect the enjoyment by the other parties of their rights under the treaty or the
performance of their obligations;
(ii) is not incompatible with the object and purpose of the treaty.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 58: Suspension of the operation of a multilateral treaty by › ¶2
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Suspension of the operation of a multilateral treaty by
exact_text:
Unless in a case falling under paragraph 1 ( a) the treaty otherwise pr ovides, the parties in
question shall notify the other parties of their intention to conclude the agreement and of those
provisions of the treaty the operation of which they intend to suspend.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 59: Termination or suspension of the operation of a treaty
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Termination or suspension of the operation of a treaty
exact_text: implied by conclusion of a later treaty

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 59: Termination or suspension of the operation of a treaty › ¶1
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Termination or suspension of the operation of a treaty
exact_text:
A treaty shall be considered as terminated if al l the parties to it conclude a later treaty relating
to the same subject matter and:
(a) it appears from the later treaty or is otherwise established that the parties intended that the matter
should be governed by that treaty; or
(b) the provisions of the later treaty are so far incomp atible with those of the earlier one that the two
treaties are not capable of being applied at the same time.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 59: Termination or suspension of the operation of a treaty › ¶2
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Termination or suspension of the operation of a treaty
exact_text:
The earlier treaty shall be considered as only suspended in operation if it appears from the later
treaty or is otherwise esta blished that such was the intention of the parties.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 60: Termination or suspension of the operation of a treaty
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Termination or suspension of the operation of a treaty
exact_text: as a consequence of its breach

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 60: Termination or suspension of the operation of a treaty › ¶1
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Termination or suspension of the operation of a treaty
exact_text:
A material breach of a bilateral treaty by one of the parties entitles the other to invoke the
breach as a ground for terminating the treaty or suspending its operation in whole or in part.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 60: Termination or suspension of the operation of a treaty › ¶2
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Termination or suspension of the operation of a treaty
exact_text:
A material breach of a multilateral treaty by one of the parties entitles:
(a) the other parties by unanimous agreement to suspend the operation of the treaty in whole or in
part or to terminate it either:
20
(i) in the relations between themselv es and the defaulting State; or
(ii) as between all the parties;
(b) a party specially affected by the breach to invoke it as a ground for suspending the operation of
the treaty in whole or in part in the relati ons between itself and the defaulting State;
(c) any party other than the defaulting State to invoke the breach as a ground for suspending the
operation of the treaty in whole or in part with respect to itself if the treaty is of such a character that a
material breach of its provisions by one party radi cally changes the position of every party with respect
to the further performance of its obligations under the treaty.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 60: Termination or suspension of the operation of a treaty › ¶3
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Termination or suspension of the operation of a treaty
exact_text:
A material breach of a treaty, for the purposes of this article, consists in:
(a) a repudiation of the treaty not sanctioned by the present Convention; or
(b) the violation of a provision essential to the accomplishment of the object or purpose of the treaty.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 60: Termination or suspension of the operation of a treaty › ¶4
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Termination or suspension of the operation of a treaty
exact_text:
The foregoing paragraphs are without prejudice to any provision in the treaty applicable in the
event of a breach.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 60: Termination or suspension of the operation of a treaty › ¶5
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Termination or suspension of the operation of a treaty
exact_text:
Paragraphs 1 to 3 do not apply to provisions relating to the protection of the human person
contained in treaties of a humanitarian character, in particular to provisions prohibiting any form of
reprisals against persons protected by such treaties.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 61: Supervening impossibility of performance › ¶1
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Supervening impossibility of performance
exact_text:
A party may invoke the impossibility of performing a treaty as a ground for terminating or
withdrawing from it if the impossibility results from the permanent disappearance or destruction of an
object indispensable for the execution of the treaty. If the impossibility is temporary, it may be invoked
only as a ground for suspending the operation of the treaty.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 61: Supervening impossibility of performance › ¶2
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Supervening impossibility of performance
exact_text:
Impossibility of performance may not be invoked by a party as a ground for terminating,
withdrawing from or suspending the operation of a treaty if the impossibility is the result of a breach by
that party either of an obligation under the treaty or of any other international obligation owed to any
other party to the treaty.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 62: Fundamental change of circumstances › ¶1
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Fundamental change of circumstances
exact_text:
A fundamental change of circumstances which has occurred with regard to those existing at the
time of the conclusion of a treaty, and which was not foreseen by the parties, may not be invoked as a
ground for terminating or withdrawing from the treaty unless:
(a) the existence of those circumstances constituted an essential basis of the consent of the parties to
be bound by the treaty; and
21
(b) the effect of the change is radically to transfor m the extent of obligations still to be performed
under the treaty.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 62: Fundamental change of circumstances › ¶2
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Fundamental change of circumstances
exact_text:
A fundamental change of circumstances may not be invoked as a ground for terminating or
withdrawing from a treaty:
(a) if the treaty establishes a boundary; or
(b) if the fundamental change is the result of a breach by the party invoking it either of an obligation
under the treaty or of any other international obligation owed to any other party to the treaty.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 62: Fundamental change of circumstances › ¶3
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Fundamental change of circumstances
exact_text:
If, under the foregoing paragraphs, a party may invoke a fundamental change of circumstances
as a ground for terminating or withdrawing from a treaty it may also invoke the change as a ground for
suspending the operation of the treaty.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 63: Severance of diplomatic or consular relations
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Severance of diplomatic or consular relations
exact_text:
The severance of diplomatic or consular relations between parties to a treaty does not affect the
legal relations established between them by the treaty except insofar as the existence of diplomatic or
consular relations is indispensable for the application of the treaty.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 64: Emergence of a new peremptory norm of general
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Emergence of a new peremptory norm of general
exact_text:
international law ("jus cogens")
If a new peremptory norm of gene ral international law emerges, a ny existing treaty which is in
conflict with that norm becomes void and terminates.

heading: Procedure to be followed with respect to invalidity,
exact_text:
A party which, under the provisions of the present Convention, invokes either a defect in its
consent to be bound by a treaty or a ground for impeaching the validity of a treaty, terminating it,
withdrawing from it or suspending its operation, mu st notify the other parties of its claim. The
notification shall indicate the measure proposed to be taken with respect to the treaty and the reasons
therefor.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 65: Procedure to be followed with respect to invalidity, › ¶2
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Procedure to be followed with respect to invalidity,
exact_text:
If, after the expiry of a period which, except in cases of special urgency, shall not be less than
three months after the receipt of the notification, no party has raised any objection, the party making the
notification may carry out in the manner provided in article 67 the measure which it has proposed.
22

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 65: Procedure to be followed with respect to invalidity, › ¶3
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Procedure to be followed with respect to invalidity,
exact_text:

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 65: Procedure to be followed with respect to invalidity, › ¶4
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Procedure to be followed with respect to invalidity,

Nothing in the foregoing paragraphs shall affect the rights or obligations of the parties under

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 65: Procedure to be followed with respect to invalidity, › ¶5
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Procedure to be followed with respect to invalidity,
exact_text:
Without prejudice to article 45, the fact that a State has not previously made the notification

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 66: Procedures for judicial settleme nt, arbitration and conciliation
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Procedures for judicial settleme nt, arbitration and conciliation
exact_text:
If, under paragraph 3 of article 65, no solution has been reached within a period of 12 months
following the date on which the objection was raised, the following procedures shall be followed:
(a) any one of the parties to a dispute concerning the application or the interpretation of article 53 or
64 may, by a written application, submit it to the In ternational Court of Justice for a decision unless the
parties by common consent agree to submit the dispute to arbitration;
(b) any one of the parties to a dispute concerning th e application or the interpretation of any of the
other articles in part V of the present Convention may set in motion the procedure specified in the Annex
to the Convention by submitting a request to that effect to the Secretary-General of the United Nations.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 69: Consequences of the in validity of a treaty › ¶1
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Consequences of the in validity of a treaty
exact_text:
A treaty the invalidity of which is established under the present Convention is void. The
provisions of a void treaty have no legal force.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 69: Consequences of the in validity of a treaty › ¶2
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Consequences of the in validity of a treaty
exact_text:
If acts have nevertheless been performed in reliance on such a treaty:
(a) each party may require any other party to establish as far as possible in their mutual relations the
position that would have existed if the acts had not been performed;
(b) acts performed in good faith before the invalidity was invoked are not rendered unlawful by
reason only of the invalidity of the treaty.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 69: Consequences of the in validity of a treaty › ¶3
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Consequences of the in validity of a treaty
exact_text:

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 69: Consequences of the in validity of a treaty › ¶4
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Consequences of the in validity of a treaty
exact_text:

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 70: Consequences of the termination of a treaty › ¶1
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Consequences of the termination of a treaty
exact_text:
Unless the treaty otherwise provides or the part ies otherwise agree, the termination of a treaty
under its provisions or in accordance with the present Convention:
(a) releases the parties from any oblig ation further to perform the treaty;
(b) does not affect any right, obligation or legal situation of the parties created through the execution
of the treaty prior to its termination.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 70: Consequences of the termination of a treaty › ¶2
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Consequences of the termination of a treaty
exact_text:

between that State and each of the other parties to the treaty from the date when such denunciation or
withdrawal takes effect.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 71: Consequences of the invalidity of a treaty which conflicts

exact_text:

(a) eliminate as far as possible the consequences of any act performed in reliance on any provision
which conflicts with the peremptory norm of general international law; and
24
(b) bring their mutual relations into conformity wi th the peremptory norm of general international
law.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 71: Consequences of the invalidity of a treaty which conflicts › ¶2
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Consequences of the invalidity of a treaty which conflicts
exact_text:

the treaty:
(a) releases the parties from any oblig ation further to perform the treaty;
(b) does not affect any right, obligation or legal situation of the parties created through the execution
of the treaty prior to its termination, provided that those rights, obligations or situations may thereafter
be maintained only to th e extent that their mainte nance is not in itself in conflict with the new
peremptory norm of general international law.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 72: Consequences of the suspension of the operation of a treaty › ¶1
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Consequences of the suspension of the operation of a treaty
exact_text:
Unless the treaty otherwise provides or the parties otherwise agree, the suspension of the
operation of a treaty under its provisions or in accordance with the present Convention:
(a) releases the parties between whic h the operation of the treaty is suspended from the obligation to
perform the treaty in their mutual relati ons during the period of the suspension;
(b) does not otherwise affect the legal relations between the parties established by the treaty.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties › Article 72: Consequences of the suspension of the operation of a treaty › ¶2
part: V: Inv Alidity, Termination And Suspension Of The Operation Of Treaties
heading: Consequences of the suspension of the operation of a treaty
exact_text:
During the period of the suspension the parties shall refrain from acts tending to obstruct the
resumption of the opera tion of the treaty.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part VI: Miscellaneous Provisions › Article 73: Cases of State succession, State responsibility
part: VI: Miscellaneous Provisions
heading: Cases of State succession, State responsibility
exact_text:
and outbreak of hostilities
The provisions of the present Convention shall not prejudge any question that may arise in regard
to a treaty from a succession of States or from the international responsibility of a State or from the
outbreak of hostiliti es between States.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part VI: Miscellaneous Provisions › Article 74: Diplomatic and consular relations and the
part: VI: Miscellaneous Provisions
heading: Diplomatic and consular relations and the
exact_text:
conclusion of treaties
The severance or absence of diplomatic or consular relations between two or more States does not
prevent the conclusion of treaties between those States. The conclusion of a treaty does not in itself
affect the situation in regard to diplomatic or consular relations.
25

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part VI: Miscellaneous Provisions › Article 75: Case of an aggressor State
part: VI: Miscellaneous Provisions
heading: Case of an aggressor State
exact_text:
The provisions of the present Convention are without prejudice to any obligation in relation to a
treaty which may arise for an aggressor State in consequence of measures taken in conformity with the
Charter of the United Nations with re ference to that State's aggression.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part VII: Depositaries , Notifications , › Article 76: Depositaries of treaties › ¶1
part: VII: Depositaries , Notifications ,
heading: Depositaries of treaties
exact_text:
The designation of the depositary of a treaty may be made by the negotiating States, either in
the treaty itself or in some other manner. The depositary may be one or more States, an international
organization or the chief administra tive officer of the organization.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part VII: Depositaries , Notifications , › Article 76: Depositaries of treaties › ¶2
part: VII: Depositaries , Notifications ,
heading: Depositaries of treaties
exact_text:
The functions of the depositary of a treaty ar e international in charac ter and the depositary is
under an obligation to act impartiall y in their performance. In particular, the fact that a treaty has not
entered into force between certain of the parties or that a difference has appeared between a State and a
depositary with regard to the perfo rmance of the latter's functions shall not affect that obligation.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part VII: Depositaries , Notifications , › Article 77: Functions of depositaries › ¶1
part: VII: Depositaries , Notifications ,
heading: Functions of depositaries

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part VII: Depositaries , Notifications , › Article 77: Functions of depositaries › ¶2
part: VII: Depositaries , Notifications ,
heading: Functions of depositaries
exact_text:
In the event of any difference appearing between a State and the depositary as to the
performance of the latter's functions, the depositary shall bring the question to the attention of the
signatory States and the contracting States or, where appropriate, of the competent organ of the
international organization concerned.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part VII: Depositaries , Notifications , › Article 78: Notifications and communications
part: VII: Depositaries , Notifications ,
heading: Notifications and communications
exact_text:
Except as the treaty or the present Convention otherwise provide, any notification or
communication to be made by any State under the present Convention shall:
(a) if there is no depositary, be transmitted direct to th e States for which it is intended, or if there is a
depositary, to the latter;
(b) be considered as having been made by the State in question only upon its receipt by the State to
which it was transmitted or, as the case may be, upon its receipt by the depositary;
(c) if transmitted to a depositary, be considered as received by the State for which it was intended
only when the latter State has been informed by the depositary in accordance with article 77, paragraph 1
(e).

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part VII: Depositaries , Notifications , › Article 79: Correction of errors in texts or in certified copies
part: VII: Depositaries , Notifications ,
heading: Correction of errors in texts or in certified copies
exact_text: of treaties

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part VII: Depositaries , Notifications , › Article 79: Correction of errors in texts or in certified copies › ¶1
part: VII: Depositaries , Notifications ,
heading: Correction of errors in texts or in certified copies
exact_text:
Where, after the authentication of the text of a treaty, the signatory States and the contracting
States are agreed that it contains an error, the error shall, unless they decide upon some other means of
correction, be corrected:
(a) by having the appropriate correction made in the text and causing the correction to be initialled by
duly authorized representatives;
(b) by executing or exchanging an instrument or instruments setting out the correction which it has
been agreed to make; or
(c) by executing a corrected text of the whole treaty by the same procedure as in the case of the
original text.
27

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part VII: Depositaries , Notifications , › Article 79: Correction of errors in texts or in certified copies › ¶2
part: VII: Depositaries , Notifications ,
heading: Correction of errors in texts or in certified copies
exact_text:
Where the treaty is one for which there is a depositary, the latter shall notify the signatory
States and the contracting States of the error and of the proposal to correct it and shall specify an
appropriate time-limit within which objection to the proposed correction may be raised. If, on the expiry
of the time-limit:
(a) no objection has been raised, the depositary shall make and initia l the correction in the text and
shall execute a procès-verbal of the rectification of the text and communicate a copy of it to the parties
and to the States entitled to become parties to the treaty;
(b) an objection has been raised, the depositary shall communicate the objection to the signatory
States and to the contracting States.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part VII: Depositaries , Notifications , › Article 79: Correction of errors in texts or in certified copies › ¶3
part: VII: Depositaries , Notifications ,
heading: Correction of errors in texts or in certified copies
exact_text:
The rules in paragraphs I and 2 apply also where the text has been authenticated in two or more
languages and it appears that there is a lack of concordance which the signatory States and the
contracting States agree should be corrected.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part VII: Depositaries , Notifications , › Article 79: Correction of errors in texts or in certified copies › ¶4
part: VII: Depositaries , Notifications ,
heading: Correction of errors in texts or in certified copies
exact_text:
The corrected text replaces the defective text ab initio, unless the signatory States and the
contracting States otherwise decide.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part VII: Depositaries , Notifications , › Article 79: Correction of errors in texts or in certified copies › ¶5
part: VII: Depositaries , Notifications ,
heading: Correction of errors in texts or in certified copies
exact_text:
The correction of the text of a treaty that has been registered shall be notified to the Secretariat
of the United Nations.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part VII: Depositaries , Notifications , › Article 79: Correction of errors in texts or in certified copies › ¶6
part: VII: Depositaries , Notifications ,
heading: Correction of errors in texts or in certified copies
exact_text:
Where an error is discovered in a certified copy of a treaty, the depositary shall execute a
procès-verbal specifying the rectification and communicate a copy of it to the signatory States and to the
contracting States.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part VII: Depositaries , Notifications , › Article 80: Registration and publication of treaties › ¶1
part: VII: Depositaries , Notifications ,
heading: Registration and publication of treaties
exact_text:
Treaties shall, after their entry into force, be transmitted to the Secretariat of the United Nations
for registration or filing and recording, as the case may be, and for publication.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part VII: Depositaries , Notifications , › Article 80: Registration and publication of treaties › ¶2
part: VII: Depositaries , Notifications ,
heading: Registration and publication of treaties
exact_text:
The designation of a depositary shall constitute authorization for it to perform the acts specified
in the preceding paragraph.

structural_path: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties › Part VIII: Final Provisions › Article 81: Signature
part: VIII: Final Provisions
heading: Signature
exact_text:
The present Convention shall be open for signature by all States Members of the United Nations
or of any of the specialized agencies or of the International Atomic Energy Agency or parties to the
Statute of the International Court of Justice, and by any other State invited by the General Assembly of
the United Nations to become a party to the Convention, as follows: until 30 November 1969, at the

Federal Ministry for Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Austria, and subsequently, until 30 April 1970, at
